claims.text: Elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding.
Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Depositing a FeCoNiMnCu HEA layer on top of the Cr coating will prevent premature coating failure.
The FeCoNiMnCu-over-Cr architecture will preserve protection during both normal subcritical-water operation and accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
An ATF coating should improve accident tolerance without degrading performance during normal reactor operation.
The proposed coating architecture will form a protective Cr2O3 layer.
The proposed architecture will form a high-entropy spinel coating.
The outer FeCoNiMnCu HEA layer will act as a diffusion barrier against interdiffusion at the buried Cr–Zr interface.
The FeCoNiMnCu HEA layer will act as an oxidation-resistant layer and reduce oxidation.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified cladding will have a lower oxidation rate.
Relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding, the modified cladding will have a reduced risk of premature coating failure under normal and accident conditions.
The hypothesis applies across 300–1200 °C and exposure times up to 100 hours.
Thermal stress or mechanical loading may delaminate the HEA layer.
Failure to achieve a statistically significant oxidation-rate reduction relative to unmodified Cr-coated cladding would falsify the hypothesis.
Occurrence of HEA-layer delamination during the steam oxidation test would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention places the proposed HEA layer on the outer surface of the Cr coating, whereas the mechanism assigns it a direct diffusion-barrier role at the buried Cr–Zr interface; no indirect pathway connecting this geometry to suppressed interfacial diffusion is stated.

The hypothesis covers normal subcritical-water operation and steam exposures over 300–1200 °C for up to 100 hours, but the proposed experiment specifies only a generic high-temperature steam test and does not test normal-water performance or define a temperature and duration within the stated boundary.
